topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing for the lecture, establishing the session's scope and key learning outcomes regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine standard therapeutic modalities used to eliminate tumor mass and the significant limitations imposed by systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic approaches that exploit intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and genetic deficiencies specific to cancer cells.

topics.label: Inhibiting oncogenic kinases and overcoming resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the inhibition of hyperactive oncogenic kinases and the diverse mechanisms through which cancer cells develop resistance to these targeted therapies.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeted therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how monoclonal antibodies, used either directly or as conjugates delivering cytotoxic payloads, selectively target cancer cell-surface proteins.

topics.label: Harnessing T-cell immunity against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for anti-tumor immune responses and the therapeutic strategies developed to mobilize or engineer T cells to eradicate cancer.

topics.label: Overall progress, clinical challenges, and future perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader historical progress of cancer therapy alongside the persistent clinical challenges, ethical dilemmas, and future directions in patient care.
